messages:
anya: heads up — CI image publish is red on main for the `push-artifact` job. started failing after PR #8942 landed.
ci-bot: job `push-artifact` failed on runner: registry returned 422 Unprocessable Entity during manifest PUT.
ci-bot: ```
Error: 422 Unprocessable Entity
Detail: layer digest mismatch for layer sha256:abc123... expected sha256:def456...
At: /v2/redwood/images/manifests/latest
```
vikram: fwiw, the job also shows different layer sizes between builder and final image in the log. small but consistent shift.
neil: can someone rerun the job first? maybe transient registry hiccup.
anya: rerun kicked (CI: #pull/8942/37) — still failing. same 422 and same checksum drift.
leo: pinging the PR author @marco — any build steps added that touch filesystem metadata? like touch, git checkout timestamps, or anything non-deterministic?
anya: @marco added a `COPY --from=builder /app/dist /app/dist` and the builder stage does a `git clone` when building artifacts. suspect timestamps/mtime differences.
neil: if builder includes git metadata (timestamped files) that can change layer content. can you paste the Dockerfile snippet?
anya: ```Dockerfile
FROM node:18 AS builder
WORKDIR /work
RUN git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/redwood/example-repo.git .
RUN npm ci && npm run build
FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs
COPY --from=builder /work/dist /app/dist
```
vikram: yep. `git clone` will preserve commit timestamps by default? actually it sets file mtimes to checkout time unless `-c core.utime=...` used. Builders in CI might produce different mtimes across runs.
leo: the registry compares layer digests (blob contents). If mtimes differ then tar layer bytes differ. We need deterministic pack. two quick fixes: 1) normalize mtimes in build (e.g., `find . -print0 | xargs -0 touch -d '@0'`) before creating artifacts, or 2) make the builder produce artifacts in a reproducible way (tar with --mtime).
neil: for fast triage, can someone try rebuild locally with `docker build --no-cache` and `docker save` + `sha256sum` to reproduce digest drift?
anya: i'm reproducing locally now. steps I'm running: 
```bash
docker build -t rwd/test:local -f docker/Dockerfile .
docker save rwd/test:local | sha256sum
```
anya: local run shows different sha256 sums across two consecutive builds on my laptop. confirms non-determinism.
leo: good repro. can you try a quick patch to set mtimes fixed in the builder stage? e.g. add: `RUN find /work -exec touch -t 197001010000 {} +` and rebuild.
anya: tried that. adding `RUN find /work -type f -exec touch -d '1970-01-01' {} +` made the saved image checksum stable for me.
vikram: OK let's do this as a short-term fix in the PR: normalize timestamps before copying. longer term we should add a lint in our buildimage to detect non-deterministic file mtimes.
neil: i'll open a quick follow-up PR to add a small `reproducible.sh` helper in our base builder image that normalizes mtimes and sorts file order.
leo: for the immediate CI unblock, can we merge a tiny revert or apply the touch patch to #8942? marco?
anya: marco is OOO today, but I can open the patch to their branch (permissive). created branch `fix/8942-normalize-mtime` and pushed a commit with the touch. retriggering the pipeline now.
ci-bot: retriggered job `push-artifact` (build 8942-38).
ci-bot: build succeeded, pushed manifest to registry. :tada:
neil: awesome. follow-up: create an infra ticket to add reproducible-build checks to our CI image job and document recommended builder practices.
sre-oncall: putting a note in the runbook for registry digests + common causes (timestamps, user vs root file ownership differences, gzip nondeterminism).
anya: thanks all. i'll link the follow-up PR and infra ticket in the original PR thread. :eyes:
